transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-05
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (BrightPath CISO), Tina Lopez (BrightPath CTO), Samir Patel (PM), Jordan Lee (Security Eng)

[00:00] Alex Kim: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro - im alex, ae at redwood. priya is our se, she'll run through the technical bits.
[00:22] Mark Rivera: thanks alex. we wanted to focus today on security, privacy, and data handling - specifically around prompts, retention, and whether redwood uses customer data to train models.
[00:37] Priya Shah: great, we'll cover SOC 2 and ISO stuff, sso/rbac, logging, kms/encryption, residency, and the data handling policy. caveat — i'll be a bit terse on some items, we'll share docs after.
[01:05] Tina Lopez: also interested in dedicated/private deployment options for production — we have strict HIPAA requirements.
[01:22] Priya Shah: noted. quick high level: redwood offers hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem options. security controls vary by deployment but the control plane can be customer-managed for private.
[01:45] Samir Patel: first question — does redwood ever train models on our prompts or logs? we need a clear legal & technical confirmation.
[01:58] Alex Kim: short answer: no. we do not train or fine-tune models on customer prompt data. that's part of our standard data handling policy. i'll state the policy and we'll include it in the DPA language.
[02:15] Jordan Lee: when you say "do not train", do you mean no long-term retention at all, or retained for short debug windows? what about aggregated telemetry?
[02:30] Priya Shah: we retain minimal request metadata for billing and debugging. content-level retention depends on deployment and contract: hosted api defaults to X days (we'll provide exact number), but enterprise contracts can set retention to zero or configure retention windows. aggregated telemetry is used for service health and is not tied to raw prompts.
[02:55] Mark Rivera: we need assurance about PII/PHI. any customer content classified as PHI — how is that handled?
[03:10] Priya Shah: for PHI use-cases we recommend private deployment / dedicated capacity. in redwood private, customer data remains in your VPC and we can support BYOK/BYOKMS so keys never leave your control. hosted api can be made HIPAA-ready under a BAA — we have customers operating under BAA.
[03:36] Tina Lopez: do you have an existing BAA template? we need to see the wording around training and retention.
[03:50] Alex Kim: yes, we'll send the BAA and DPA draft. action: i'll attach BAA, SOC2, and iso27001 evidence.
[04:05] Priya Shah: on encryption — data at rest is encrypted. for hosted we manage keys by default; for enterprise/private we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM connectors.
[04:30] Jordan Lee: any limitation on key rotation or access logging for KMS? we want to ensure key usage logs are visible in our audit trail.
[04:43] Priya Shah: we log KMS calls in our audit logs and can forward logs to your SIEM. for private deployments, key usage never leaves your VPC and you can retain logs per your retention policy.
[05:04] Mark Rivera: audit logs — what do you log? are prompts included?
[05:18] Priya Shah: by default audit logs include request IDs, timestamps, model used, route, and metadata. content logging (full prompts) is optional and disabled by default for hosted plans; enterprise customers can configure content logging for debugging but it's contractually controlled.
[05:41] Samir Patel: so if we enable content logging for debugging, is that stored encrypted and for how long?
[05:53] Priya Shah: encrypted at rest; retention is configurable. default hosted retention is 30 days (we'll confirm exact), but enterprise legal can set shorter or zero retention. logs can be exported to your S3 or SIEM.
[06:12] Tina Lopez: can we get a signed attestation that redwood won't use our data to train public models?
[06:22] Alex Kim: yes, we provide contractual language in the DPA that explicitly states we will not use customer content to train models. operationally, we have internal controls to prevent model training on customer data. we'll include that attestation.
[06:40] Jordan Lee: what about telemetry and model feedback loops? do you use aggregated signals across customers to improve model prompts/algorithms? any chance of leakage?
[06:53] Priya Shah: aggregated telemetry is used for product improvements, but it's de-identified and not tied to raw customer prompts. we have controls to prevent cross-customer data leakage. for customers with strict requirements, we can opt out of telemetry-based improvements in contract.
[07:16] Mark Rivera: SOC 2 and ISO — can you summarize which attestations you have current?
[07:26] Alex Kim: we completed SOC 2 type II last quarter — we'll attach the report redacted. we're in process of ISO27001 certification — target Q1 next year, but we already operate many of the controls.
[07:44] Tina Lopez: do you have evidence of penetration testing and third-party assessments?
[07:51] Priya Shah: yes, annual pentests and automated code scanning reports. we'll share summary findings and remediation timelines where permissible.
[08:03] Samir Patel: residency — we want all prod data kept in us-east and us-west only. is that supported?
[08:12] Priya Shah: yes, region pinning is available for enterprise and private deployments. hosted customers can also restrict region in their tenant settings for an additional control.
[08:26] Mark Rivera: RBAC and SSO — we need SCIM and SAML support and role-based access controls integrated with our identity provider.
[08:37] Priya Shah: we support SAML SSO, OIDC, and SCIM provisioning. RBAC is configurable with granular roles: admin, billing, developer, read-only, etc. we can map to your groups.
[08:51] Jordan Lee: audit trail of admin actions — can we capture user actions like model pinning, rollout changes, and key rotations?
[09:02] Priya Shah: yes, admin actions are recorded in the audit log with actor, timestamp, and action details. for private deployments we can push logs to your SIEM or S3.
[09:18] Mark Rivera: one concern is debugging: our SREs want occasional transcripts for debugging model outputs. fine, but we need a process to request and a TTL on stored transcripts.
[09:31] Alex Kim: that's standard. we'll implement gated access, approvals, and short retention windows. these are contractually enforceable for enterprise deals.
[09:44] Samir Patel: encryption in transit — TLS version and ciphers?
[09:50] Priya Shah: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers; we can provide a cipher suite list in the security pack.
[10:00] Tina Lopez: logging format — do you include unique request IDs we can correlate across services?
[10:06] Priya Shah: yes request_id is present in headers and logs to correlate. we'll show an example log line in the docs.
[10:18] Mark Rivera: about KMS again — if we supply our own key, do you ever get access to plaintext?
[10:27] Priya Shah: no, with BYOK the key operations happen in your KMS and we only get ciphertext. for private deployments keys remain in your environment. we'll document exact flow.
[10:40] Alex Kim: quick demo note — priya will show config snippets in the docs we send.
[10:46] Priya Shah: yes, i'll include terraform and policy examples.
[11:00] Samir Patel: can you confirm incident response SLAs and notification process for security incidents?
[11:08] Alex Kim: we have an incident response playbook, 24/7 paging for Sev1, incident notifications within defined windows — we'll include the incident response summary and contact process.
[11:22] Jordan Lee: do you perform background checks on engineers who may see logs?
[11:28] Priya Shah: yes, we have employee background checks, access controls, and least privilege applied. access to customer content is restricted and logged.
[11:43] Mark Rivera: curious about sub-processors and third-party cloud vendors — who's involved?
[11:50] Alex Kim: we use cloud providers (AWS/GCP) for infrastructure and a small set of monitoring vendors; SOC2 report lists subservice orgs. we'll provide the list.
[12:05] Tina Lopez: interplay with model selection — if you route to open models or vendor-managed models, are there additional risks?
[12:16] Priya Shah: model routing can be policy-driven. for regulated workloads we can restrict to vetted models and dedicated infra; policy prevents fallback to external models that don't meet compliance.
[12:32] Samir Patel: about model outputs that might include PHI — do you perform redaction or filters?
[12:40] Priya Shah: we offer content filters and PII-detection tooling; for high-risk deployments we recommend client-side redaction or proxying through your preprocessor.
[12:55] Mark Rivera: regarding logs forwarded to our SIEM — can you apply tokenization or hashing for PII fields before forwarding?
[13:05] Priya Shah: yes we can implement tokenization or pseudonymization in the export pipeline; we'll include example configs.
[13:20] Alex Kim: open item: we'll provide exact retention numbers and a redacted SOC2 report.
[13:28] Priya Shah: operational note: we have a kill switch to purge stored content on contract termination or on-demand if negotiated.
[13:40] Jordan Lee: is there a cost delta for private deployment or BYOK?
[13:46] Alex Kim: yes there is a premium for dedicated/private deployments and BYOK integrations; pricing details will be included in the sales quote.
[14:00] Mark Rivera: can we get a formal attestation that customer data won't be used to train models and that any content used for debugging is under strict access controls?
[14:12] Alex Kim: yes — contractual attestation + internal controls. we'll include language in the DPA and BAA if HIPAA applies.
[14:28] Samir Patel: last technical Q — do you maintain separate model instances per tenant in dedicated deployments?
[14:36] Priya Shah: dedicated pools can be isolated at the tenant level and we can pin models; KV caches and runtimes are isolated for tenant workloads.
[14:50] Tina Lopez: sounds good — timeline wise we're targeting pilot in Q1. can you support a compliance checklist we can give procurement?
[14:59] Alex Kim: yes we'll send a compliance checklist and a proposed pilot plan.
[15:08] Priya Shah: i'll follow up with configuration examples for KMS and VPC peering.
[15:18] Mark Rivera: thanks. one more: who to contact on infra/ops side during pilot?
[15:24] Alex Kim: i'll be primary AE contact, priya will be se lead; we'll loop in our customer reliability engineer for the pilot.
[15:36] Samir Patel: okay thanks y'all.
[15:40] Alex Kim: recap and next steps — we'll send SOC2/ISO docs, BAA/DPA drafts, KMS integration guide, data retention options, and schedule a VPC deep dive.
[15:54] Priya Shah: action items noted.
[16:00] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcript with a few mis-recognitions ("KMS" sometimes seen as "K M S", "SOC 2" sometimes "SOC two"). Links referenced during call: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2 (SOC2 redacted), https://redwood.example.com/docs/kms-integration (KMS guide).
